title: Promotion
summary: A pawn that reaches the last rank turns into a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Learn how promotion works and why the queen is usually the choice.

steps.title: From pawn to queen
steps.text: When a pawn reaches the far end of the board, it must be promoted: you swap it for a queen, rook, bishop or knight of your color. You can even have two or three queens at once. Almost always you pick a queen, because she is the strongest piece.
steps.narration: Every pawn dreams of reaching the far side of the board. When it does, it transforms into any piece you like, and almost always that's a brand new queen. [move]

steps.title: Crown your pawn
steps.prompt: Your pawn is one step from the end. Promote it to a queen.
steps.hint: Push the pawn to e8 and choose the queen.
steps.success: A new queen, and with check too. Black's rook is no match for her.
steps.narration: Your pawn on e7 is one step from glory, and nothing can stop it. Push it forward and pick the queen.

steps.title: Promote by capturing
steps.prompt: The square in front of your pawn is blocked. Find another way to promote.
steps.hint: Pawns capture diagonally, and a capture onto the last rank promotes too.
steps.success: Pawn takes the rook and becomes a queen in the same move. You won a rook and gained a queen.
steps.narration: Black's knight blocks your pawn's path. But a pawn can also promote by capturing diagonally onto the last rank. Is there anything to capture?

steps.title: Quick check
steps.question: Your pawn reaches the last rank. Which of these can it NOT become?

options.why: Each side has exactly one king. A pawn may become a queen, rook, bishop or knight.
You may have more than one queen. Promoting to a queen is the usual choice.
Promoting to a knight is allowed, and once in a while it is the best choice, for example when it gives a winning check.

steps.narration: Last question. A pawn can become almost anything when it reaches the end. Almost. Which piece is off limits?
